1.why: All eight screens are static cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs; only a text 'Logs' panel updates in place.

2.why: Each step has one bold dark-blue heading and a single primary blue button, and focused fields get a yellow outline, though the black Logs panel competes for attention with equal visual weight.

3.why: Each page shows only one short task (enter email, enter code, set password) so the required field and action button are immediately visible, but the developer-oriented log panel adds irrelevant content to scan.

4.why: Steps are guided one at a time, but the user must carry the long recovery code and the 6-digit code across screens and remember the 12-character/uppercase/number/symbol password rules while typing.

5.why: No password manager integration, autofill hint, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Nothing saved or familiar is surfaced — no remembered email, no masked account hint, no previously used device recognition; only the raw echoed values in the log panel.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain and legible in a sans-serif font at good contrast (e.g. 'Enter the six-digit verification code...'), although the log text is small monospace jargon like 'SIMULATED MFA DELIVERY'.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the eight screenshots — only success/status messages — so there is no evidence of error messages describing a problem and its fix.

9.why: The password screen states rules ('12 or more characters, including uppercase...') but no field shows a placeholder or worked example of what to type, and no example format is given for the codes.

10.why: Only the two recovery routes ('Send recovery instructions' vs 'Enter a recovery code manually') are offered; there is no visible choice of password, code, or face/biometric login as the statement describes.

11.why: Each screen presents at most two or three buttons and one or two fields, so the user is never faced with many simultaneous options.

12.why: Outcomes are stated after actions — the green 'secure recovery instructions have been prepared' line and the 'Password updated' confirmation page — though intermediate code verification gives no explicit success message beyond moving on.

13.why: Some helpful hints exist (privacy note, password rules, 'Keep your account safe' panel), but there is no progress indicator, step count, or contextual tip explaining what a recovery code is or where to find it.

14.why: A 'Back' button appears on the code-verification step and 'Start another recovery' at the end, but most steps offer no visible retry, resend-code, or cancel option.

15.why: Header, card layout, typography, button colours, safety panel and log panel remain identical across all eight steps, giving a highly consistent learnable design.
